source: arXiv:2409.09561 Mansfield & Spradlin, 'On Unitarity of the Hypergeometric Amplitude' (38 pp)
location: Theorem 11 and Eq. (5.16), Section 5.3 'Regge Asymptotics', p.25-27 of the arXiv PDF
paraphrase: For the w=0 hypergeometric family, the large-n Regge asymptotics of the partial-wave coefficient at odd Delta = n-j carries the overall factor (2r + m^2 + 1): asymptotic positivity on the l=n-1 trajectory requires 2r + m^2 + 1 > 0, i.e. r > -(1+m^2)/2. Obtained via double-contour methods, asymptotic only, w=0 only.
limitations: Asymptotic statement (n->inf), w=0 slice only; our exact finite-n law reduces to the same critical line on that slice.
relevance: External control for the left-edge theorem: independent method reproduces the same critical combination 2r+mu0+1 at w=0. Our result: exact at every n, and extends to w != 0 (untouched by them).

source: arXiv:2408.03362 / Phys. Rev. D 111, 086034 (2025), Cheung, Hillman, Remmen
location: Eqs. (4),(6),(7) p.3 (family, residues); Positivity section p.6 (odd waves vanish; D=4 positive all lambda; D>=9 bounds lambda from below, Fig. 1)
paraphrase: Level truncation of M and dM/dt forces squared residues; crossing yields the one-parameter lambda-family with mu(n)=(n+lam-1)/lam; VS at lambda=1; positivity mapped numerically at finite depth.
limitations: Their positivity is finite-depth numerical; no closed-form boundary given.
